# Subscription Semantic Layer

A metrics layer for subscription analytics: dbt models, documented definitions,
and a dashboard — built around the idea that the hard part of subscription
analytics is not SQL, it is agreeing on what the numbers mean.

**The data is synthetic.** It is generated by `data/generate.py` with twelve
real-world ambiguities deliberately injected, because a metrics layer is only
interesting if there is something for it to disambiguate.

---

## The three findings

**1. Realized revenue is 77.0% of tracked revenue.**
Tracked is gross at purchase; realized nets out refunds and store commission.
Anyone forecasting cash from tracked revenue is over by roughly 23%.

**2. Realized revenue for recent periods is provisional and falls over time.**
Refunds land a median of 37 days after purchase (p90: 65 days). Settled periods
realize at 77.0%; periods still inside the refund window show 74.3% and will
keep dropping. This is the trap — a dashboard showing last month's realized
revenue is showing a number that has not finished changing. The layer encodes
this as an `is_settled` flag rather than leaving it to be rediscovered.

**3. 8.4% of churn is involuntary.**
Blended, churn looks like one retention problem. Split into voluntary
(cancelled) and involuntary (payment failed), it is a product problem and a
payments problem, with different owners. ~40% of billing retries recover, so
subscribers in retry have not actually churned.

**4. Without the semantic layer, 11 of 12 business questions get a wrong or
under-specified answer.**
The verification harness runs each question twice — once with the query a
competent analyst writes from the raw schema, once with the documented
definition. Largest error: **25.2%** (realized revenue, from omitting store
commission). See [`verification/REPORT.md`](verification/REPORT.md).

---

## What's here

```
data/generate.py           synthetic data generator, 12 injected ambiguities
data/validate_seeds.py     asserts all 12 are present before anything claims them
semantic/DEFINITIONS.md    the metric definitions — the centerpiece
models/staging/            typed, lightly-cleaned source views
models/marts/              the definitions as enforced SQL
macros/always_filters.sql  sandbox + test-account exclusion, defined once
verification/              naive-vs-documented harness + generated report
dashboard/                 Evidence app (markdown + SQL)
_archive/                  superseded parallel implementation, kept not deleted
```

Every metric in `DEFINITIONS.md` has four parts: definition, SQL, gotchas, and
**what it does not say**. The fourth is the one that matters — metrics without it
get misused.

## The twelve injected ambiguities

| # | Condition | Observed | Metric it complicates |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sandbox transactions | 2.99% | every metric (always-filter) |
| 2 | Internal test accounts | 1.55% of subscribers | every metric (always-filter) |
| 3 | Late-landing refunds | median 37d, p90 65d | realized revenue |
| 4 | Sub-hour trial cancels | 8.4% of trial starts | trial starts |
| 5 | Repeat trialers | 460 subscribers | trial starts ≠ unique users |
| 6 | Billing retry / grace period | 40 / 57 concurrent | active subscribers |
| 7 | Voluntary vs involuntary churn | 91.6% / 8.4% | churn |
| 8 | Annual plans | 17.8% of transactions | MRR amortization |
| 9 | Cross-platform identity | 1,163 humans, >1 ID | subscriber ≠ person |
| 10 | FX drift | BRL 0.1967 → 0.1672 | revenue by country |
| 11 | Mid-period product changes | 741 events | revenue attribution |
| 12 | Mixed commission rates | 2.9% / 15% / 30% | realized revenue |

`validate_seeds.py` asserts each of these is actually present. No claim in the
documentation rests on an unverified condition.

## Running it

```bash
# 1. generate seeds and load DuckDB
python3 data/generate.py --subscribers 20000 --seed 42
python3 data/validate_seeds.py          # confirms all 12 conditions present

# 2. build the models
pip install dbt-core dbt-duckdb duckdb
dbt run --profiles-dir .                # 11 models

# 3. dashboard
#    requires the Evidence CLI: https://docs.evidence.studio/cli
cd dashboard && evidence dev

# 4. verification harness
python3 verification/run_harness.py
python3 verification/run_harness.py --format md > verification/REPORT.md
```

The dbt models are warehouse-portable — DuckDB is used here so the project is
self-contained and reproducible from a clone. The same models run on Snowflake
with a profile change.

## Notes on scope

Deliberately **not** modelled, and listed rather than silently ignored:
proration on upgrades, partial refunds, chargebacks, and tax. Each would change
realized revenue. See the "Open questions" section of `DEFINITIONS.md`.

The `test_accounts` table has to be maintained by hand and will go stale. Any
metric depending on it inherits that staleness — an unexplained jump in
subscriber counts should be checked there first.
